steps.what: Hire workers who can locate people with specified attributes and talents
Supervise sourcing workers and review how they locate suitable talent

tasks.design: Keep hiring decisions and worker supervision human, using existing {ATS}, {DOCS} and {PROJECT} records. The talent director evaluates sourcing capability and guides the workers' actual practice rather than dispatching them through an automated suitability score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selecting and supervising sourcing workers depends on professional judgement and trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native hiring and project records already support this workflow.
tasks.still_hard: A worker's understanding of a nuanced brief and their treatment of prospective talent require direct oversight.
tasks.human_edge: The talent director develops sourcing workers' judgement and addresses weak practice.
tasks.altitude: Hiring and supervision effort and delegated rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Delegate talent sourcing against a creative brief
reach.learn: Clear delegation and review of sourcing practice

evidence.claim: Hiring sourcing workers and supervising their judgement are human management activities; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is the talent director's hiring and supervision of sourcing workers, excluding workers' search execution, performer auditioning and final casting. Workers' time is outside the focal denominator and no transfer is proposed.

Existing production management supplies the approved sourcing brief and hiring authority before s1. Candidates provide applications during normal participation. Talent director evaluates and records hiring terms within s1's 40 hours; no free structured worker rating is assumed.

Workers produce progress accounts and sourcing results only after hiring and doing their existing assigned work, before the relevant s2 review. Director elicits, checks and records guidance within s2's 60 hours; no free structured completion or suitability flag is assumed.
Keep current native records and existing specialist checks. No automated selection, tracking or new process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Scope of the talent director's hiring authority
How sourcing workers are engaged and supervised
research_questions: Can sourcing workers explain the brief, escalation route and expected treatment of prospective performers?

already_counted.description: Evaluate and hire workers and supervise their sourcing practice

incremental.description: No changed workflow or new upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Exact worker identity, role, engagement terms and approved hiring authority checked before commitment; changes require renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental focal upkeep=0. Hiring judgement and supervision retain full effort; no sourcing-worker labour is claimed as a focal saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Teach acting classes through demonstration, practice, observation and individual feedback

tasks.design: Keep acting instruction human, with existing exercise material in {DOCS} where needed. The teacher demonstrates, watches practice and adapts feedback to each student's performance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learning depends on coached practice and the teacher's response to actual performance.
tasks.enabler_now: Current teaching arrangements already support the work; no new automation is required.
tasks.still_hard: Students need different explanations and feedback as their confidence and technique develop.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher recognises a useful next exercise and helps a student try it safely and expressively.
tasks.altitude: Teaching time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coach performers toward a scene's creative intent

evidence.claim: Acting instruction requires observation, demonstration and responsive coaching; no saving is claimed for replacing that interaction.

assumptions: Boundary is conducting acting classes, excluding enrolment, scheduling, marketing courses and producing general lesson materials. No clerical baseline is added to the teaching task.

Teacher supplies exercises through existing preparation; students produce performances during class before receiving the corresponding feedback. Observing, interpreting and capturing any feedback are within the retained 100 hours; no free structured performance score is assumed.
Keep current native teaching resources. No model assessment, recording or new process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether students need particular accessibility arrangements
research_questions: Do students understand and demonstrate a useful next step after individual feedback?

already_counted.description: Demonstrate exercises, observe practice and provide acting feedback

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Human instruction and observation retain full time; no class administration is invented to create a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Locate extras, stand-ins and photo doubles

steps.what: Locate potential performers, extras, stand-ins and photo doubles against the production brief
Contact performers or agents to establish availability and clarify suitability for background scenes or doubles

tasks.design: Keep source assessment and direct contact human, using current performer records in {DOCS} and existing phone or {EMAIL} channels. The talent director clarifies the production need with performers or agents rather than inferring attributes from images or automatically ranking people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding an appropriate stand-in or background performer depends on precise production context and current personal availability.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native performer records support source lookup; they do not remove the need for contextual checking and contact.
tasks.still_hard: Records may be stale and a superficially similar candidate may not meet practical scene requirements.
tasks.human_edge: The talent director understands the brief and can discover important constraints through respectful conversation.
tasks.altitude: Sourcing and relationship effort remain unchanged; no new selection authority is gained.

reach.task: Clarify background scene and stand-in requirements
reach.learn: Scene feasibility and specific production constraints

evidence.claim: Locating background performers and doubles combines contextual assessment with direct contact; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is locating and contacting potential background performers or doubles, excluding auditions, final casting, formal booking and general audition invitation administration. A shared contact action must have one owner.

Production directors produce the sourcing brief through existing creative work; performers and agents provide existing records. Talent director checks relevance in s1's 45 hours without free structured suitability labels.

Performers or agents produce current availability and clarification only in response to s2 contact, after the shortlist. The talent director elicits, verifies and records it within s2's 55 hours; no earlier step assumes those answers already exist.
Keep native records and current communication. No image analysis, automated ranking or new capture process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How complete and current performer records are
Which production requirements need direct specialist confirmation
research_questions: Does the sourcing brief identify the practical requirements that contacts must clarify before casting?

already_counted.description: Assess existing sources and contact performers or agents to clarify current information

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Contextual sourcing and direct contact keep full time; no automated attribute inference or counterpart time saving is assumed.
